```{r version-info, include=FALSE}
pknca_ver <- as.character(packageVersion("PKNCA"))
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
This book was built against **PKNCA `r pknca_ver`**. Examples are verified against that version. For the function reference, see the [pkgdown site](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/reference/index.html).
:::

**PKNCA** is an R package for automated noncompartmental analysis (NCA). It calculates PK parameters (AUC, Cmax, half-life, clearance, volume, and many more) from concentration-time data, supports IV and extravascular routes, urine excretion, sparse sampling, multiple-dose designs, and CDISC-aligned output. This book documents PKNCA ≥ 0.13.0 with runnable examples throughout. For the package authors' own orientation material, see the vignettes [Introduction to PKNCA and Usage Instructions](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v01-introduction-and-usage.html) and [PKNCA – an R package for noncompartmental analysis of pharmacokinetic data](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v31-FDA-introduction.html).

## What is NCA?

**Noncompartmental analysis (NCA)** derives pharmacokinetic parameters directly from observed data using numerical integration — no compartmental model assumptions required. NCA is used to answer:

- How much drug was absorbed? → **AUC**
- How fast was drug eliminated? → **half-life**, **λz**
- How high did concentrations get? → **Cmax**
- How quickly was drug cleared? → **CL**
- How widely did drug distribute? → **Vz**

## Core workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Concentration<br/>data frame"] --> B[PKNCAconc]
    C["Dose<br/>data frame"] --> D[PKNCAdose]
    B --> E[PKNCAdata]
    D --> E
    F["Intervals<br/>specification"] -.->|optional override| E
    E --> G[pk.nca]
    G --> H[PKNCAresults]
    H --> I[summary]
    H --> J[as.data.frame]
```

| Object | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `PKNCAconc` | Concentration data location and grouping |
| `PKNCAdose` | Dose amount, time, and route |
| `PKNCAdata` | Parameters and analysis intervals |
| `PKNCAresults` | Computed NCA parameters, units, exclusion flags |

The vignette [Computing NCA Parameters for Theophylline](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v02-example-theophylline.html) runs this exact pipeline end-to-end.

## Route-specific parameters

| Parameter | IV | Extravascular |
|---|---|---|
| C0 (extrapolated at t=0) | ✓ | — |
| Cmax | ✓ | ✓ |
| Tmax | ✓ | ✓ |
| AUClast / AUCinf | ✓ | ✓ |
| Half-life / λz | ✓ | ✓ |
| CL (true clearance) | ✓ | — (apparent: CL/F) |
| Vz (volume) | ✓ | — (apparent: Vz/F) |
| Bioavailability (F) | — (serves as reference) | ✓ |

For bioavailability, IV data serve as the reference against which extravascular exposure is compared.

## What's new in 0.13.0

PKNCA 0.13.0 is a large release; the package [NEWS](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/news/index.html) lists every change. Changes that alter default results are marked **breaking**.

- **Automatic intervals rebuilt (breaking)** — when no intervals are given, `PKNCAdata()` builds them from the dosing regimen: a single dose gets one interval from the dose to infinity with `start_predose_conc0` imputation, and repeated dosing gets an interval between each pair of sampled consecutive doses, chosen segment by segment when the regimen changes. `auto.interval.method = "legacy"` restores the previous behavior. See [Automatic Intervals and Dosing Regimens](user/auto-intervals.qmd).
- **Dosing-regimen detection** — `find.dose.regimen()` and a reworked `find.tau()`, nominal times, and time units for `tau`.
- **Secondary parameters in one run** — bioavailability, accumulation and metabolite ratios, and renal clearance computed across intervals and groups with `interval_id`/`*_ref` columns and `interval_add_secondary()`. See [Secondary Parameters](user/secondary-parameters.qmd).
- **Bioavailability renamed (breaking)** — `f` is now `f.obs`, alongside `f.pred`, `f.last`, and the `f.int.*` family.
- **Bioequivalence** — the `be_*` functions assess average, scaled, and narrow-therapeutic-index bioequivalence and descriptive comparisons. See [Bioequivalence](user/bioequivalence.qmd).
- **Sparse NCA unified (breaking names)** — sparse results use the standard parameter names (`auclast`, `aucinf.obs`, `aucivinf.obs`, …) with `_se` and `_df` companions; the AUC to infinity includes the uncertainty of λz by the delta method; IV bolus, batch designs, and `sparse_bootstrap()` are supported. See [Sparse PK Sampling](user/sparse.qmd).
- **Dose-aware partial AUCs (breaking)** — every `aucint`/`aumcint` parameter is dose-aware; the `.dose` variants are retired.
- **Data quality checks** — `pknca_missing_samples()` and the `exclude_nca_tmax_coverage()` exclusion rule. See [Data Quality Checks](user/data-quality.qmd).
- **Date-time data and CDISC output** — POSIXct/Date times, SDTM time references (PPSTINT, PPENINT, PPTPTREF, PPRFTDTC), PPGRPID, and `as.data.frame(results, out_format = "cdisc")`. See [Date-Time Data and Time References](user/datetime.qmd) and [Regulatory & CDISC](user/regulatory.qmd).
- **Half-life** — Tobit regression through the full `pk.nca()` pipeline (`PKNCAconc(lloq = )`), point-selection controls, `lambda.z.corrxy`, and `get_halflife_fit()`/`get_halflife_curve()` for plotting the fit.
- **Interval tools** — `pknca_interval_table()`, `pknca_presets()`, `pknca_parameter_table()`, and the `interval_add_param()` family.
- **Expanded parameters** — the `cl.*`, `kel.*`, `mrt.*`, `vss.*`, and `vz.*` families, `aumciv*`, `aumcint*`, `tmin`, and excretion parameters (`volpk`, `ermax`, `ertmax`, `ertlst`, `clr.*.dn`).
- **Post-processing and units** — `normalize()`/`normalize_by_col()`, and `pknca_units_table()` built automatically by `PKNCAdata()`.
